title: A Survey of Time Series Data Forecasting Methods Based on Deep Learning
authors: Chen, J.; Chen, T.; Wang, Y.; Wang, L.
venue: Journal of Basic and Applied Research International
tldr: Reviews deep learning methods for time series forecasting including RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs, CNNs, and Transformers with experimental comparisons on the ETT dataset.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional machine learning methods and statistical models struggle to handle massive time series datasets generated by IoT sensors. Deep learning offers alternatives but a comprehensive survey comparing architectures is needed.
approach: Reviews common features of time series data, relevant datasets (ETT, Weather, Electricity, Traffic, ILI, TE), and evaluation metrics (MSE, MAE, RMSE, MAPE).
Categorizes deep learning methods into RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs, CNNs, and Transformer-based models.
Conducts prediction experiments on deep learning models using the ETT dataset.
Evaluates performance using MAE and MSE metrics.
Analyzes strengths and weaknesses of each architecture for time series forecasting.
findings: RNNs with memory capabilities excel at capturing long-term dependencies in time series.
Transformers with self-attention mechanisms achieve superior performance for parallel computation and long-range dependencies.
LSTM and GRU effectively solve vanishing gradient problems in long-sequence processing.
Autoformer introduces decomposition architecture integrating sequence decomposition into the Transformer.
CNNs struggle to capture long-range dependencies despite deep convolutional layers.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This survey provides a structured comparison of deep learning architectures for time series forecasting, covering RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs, CNNs, and Transformers. It catalogs standard evaluation metrics, datasets, and architectural variations including Autoformer's decomposition approach. The paper serves as a reference for selecting forecasting architectures based on data characteristics and task requirements.
directly_justifies: LSTM solves vanishing gradient through forget, input, and output gates.
Transformers achieve superior long-range dependency capture via self-attention.
Autoformer integrates sequence decomposition directly into the Transformer architecture.
limits: Survey nature provides no novel empirical contributions.
Limited experimental validation on only the ETT dataset.
Does not cover emerging architectures like Mamba or state-space models.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains was conducted. Topic 6.B (Forecasting Algorithms) was rated high as the survey comprehensively covers deep learning methods for time series forecasting directly applicable to spending data prediction. Topic 14.B (ML Model Serving) was rated low as deployment considerations are mentioned only in passing. Topics 1.x-5.x, 7.x-14.A, and 14.C were rejected as the paper is a general methodology survey not addressing personal finance, budgeting, user behavior, or mobile design.

limitations: Limited experimental validation on only the ETT dataset.
Does not cover recent advances like state-space models or Mamba architecture. [unacknowledged]
Survey lacks quantitative comparison tables across all methods reviewed.
